name: Anthony van Dyck

summary.text: Sir Anthony van Dyck was a Flemish Baroque artist, who became the leading court painter in England after success in the Spanish Netherlands and Italy.
summary.title: Anthony van Dyck

609576: The Crowning with Thorns is an oil painting on canvas created ca. 1618–1620 by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck. He produced it aged 20 during his first Antwerp period, when he was the main studio assistant and pupil of Peter Paul Rubens.
3399430: Portrait of Gaston, Duke of Orléans is an oil on canvas portrait of Gaston, Duke of Orléans by Anthony van Dyck, painted in 1632 or 1634. At the time its subject had fled France and was living in exile in his mother Marie de Medici's court in Brussels.
Portrait of Gaston, Duke of Orléans
3614563: Cupid and Psyche is an oil on canvas painting by Anthony van Dyck. It is now in the British Royal Collection and shown in Kensington Palace.
3630734: The Self-portrait of 1613–1614 is the first surviving self-portrait by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck, showing him aged about fifteen. At that date he was still working for Hendrick van Balen but was about to join Peter Paul Rubens's studio.
3630737: The Self-portrait is an oil on canvas painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck. It is held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, in New York.
3630749: Self-portrait with Sir Endymion Porter is a self-portrait by Anthony van Dyck, showing him with his patron Sir Endymion Porter.
3630756: Self-Portrait with a Sunflower is a self-portrait by Anthony van Dyck, a Flemish Baroque artist from Antwerp, then in the Spanish Netherlands. The oil on canvas painting is generally between 1632 and 1633.
3663791: The Betrayal of Christ is a c. 1618-20 painting by Anthony van Dyck. He also produced two other versions of the same subject at around the same time, now in Madrid and Minneapolis.
The Betrayal of Christ (van Dyck, Bristol)
3663792: The Betrayal of Christ is a c. 1620 painting by the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck now at Museo del Prado in Madrid. He also produced two other versions of the same subject at around the same time, now in Bristol and Minneapolis.
The Betrayal of Christ (van Dyck, Madrid)
3663793: The Betrayal of Christ is a 1620 painting by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Minneapolis Institute of Arts. He also produced two other versions of the same subject at around the same time, now in Bristol and Madrid.
The Betrayal of Christ (van Dyck, Minneapolis)
3761428: Christ on the Cross between the Two Criminals or The Thrust of the Spear is a 1620 painting currently attributed to Anthony van Dyck. It depicts an episode during the Crucifixion of Jesus in which a Roman soldier pierces Christ's side with a spear to make sure he is dead.
3819218: Theodosius and Saint Ambrose is a painting by Peter Paul Rubens, with assistance from his main pupil Anthony van Dyck, executed c. 1615–1616. It is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
3842509: Madonna and Child with Two Donors or The Madonna of the Two Donors is a 1630 painting by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Louvre, in Paris.
Madonna and Child with Two Donors (van Dyck)
3936370: Rest on the Flight into Egypt is a 1630 painting by Anthony van Dyck, probably commissioned by a layman. Featuring the Holy Family of Joseph, Mary, and Jesus, it was owned by Maximilian II Emanuel, Elector of Bavaria and is now in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich.
Rest on the Flight into Egypt (van Dyck)
3937427: Portrait of Cardinal Guido Bentivoglio is an oil on canvas painting of Guido Bentivoglio by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Galleria Palatina in Florence. It was painted around 1623 during the artist's stay in Italy - Bentivoglio had links to the artist's native Flanders.
3937435: Equestrian Portrait of Thomas Francis, Prince of Carignano is a 1634 painting by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Galleria Sabauda in Turin. It shows Thomas Francis, Prince of Carignano on a prancing horse, as an allegory of his holding the reins of command even in difficult moments.
Equestrian Portrait of Thomas Francis, Prince of Carignano
3937446: The Lomellini Family is a portrait painting by the Flemish Baroque painter Anthony van Dyck. A group portrait of a landed Genoese family, it is in the Scottish National Gallery in Edinburgh.
3937481: The Equestrian Portrait of Charles I is a large oil painting on canvas by Anthony van Dyck, showing Charles I on horseback. Charles I had become King of England, Scotland and Ireland in 1625 on the death of his father James I, and Van Dyck became Charles's Principal Painter in Ordinary in 1632.
3937482: Charles I with M. de St Antoine is an oil painting on canvas by the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck, depicting Charles I on horseback, accompanied by his riding master, Pierre Antoine Bourdon, Seigneur de St Antoine.
Charles I with M. de St Antoine
3937485: Charles I at the Hunt, also known under its French title Le Roi à la chasse, is an oil-on-canvas portrait of Charles I of England by Anthony van Dyck, dated to c. 1635, and now in the Louvre Museum in Paris.
3937501: The Portrait of Cornelis van der Geest is a panel painting by Anthony van Dyck from about 1620. The original panel and painting were expanded by other artists.
Portrait of Cornelis van der Geest
3937534: Portrait of Francisco de Moncada is a 1634 oil on canvas portrait of Francisco de Moncada by Anthony van Dyck, commissioned simultaneously with the equestrian portrait of the same subject now in the Louvre. Since at least 1720 it has been in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
3937593: Lord John Stuart and His Brother, Lord Bernard Stuart is a large oil painting by Anthony van Dyck, executed c. 1638.
Lord John Stuart and His Brother, Lord Bernard Stuart
3937775: Equestrian Portrait of Francisco de Moncada is a 1634 oil on canvas painting by Antony van Dyck, one of his most famous portraits, now INV 1240 in Room 850 (d) of the Louvre Museum, which acquired it from the Palazzo Braschi in Rome in 1798.
Equestrian Portrait of Francisco de Moncada
3948607: Samson and Delilah is a 1630 painting by Anthony van Dyck. Like his 1620 version of the subject, it is in the style of his former master Peter Paul Rubens.
3948693: Saint Ambrose barring Theodosius from Milan Cathedral is a painting of c. 1619–20 by Anthony van Dyck in the National Gallery, in London.
Saint Ambrose barring Theodosius from Milan Cathedral
3949246: Saint Rosalie Interceding for the Plague-stricken of Palermo is a painting of 1624 by Anthony van Dyck, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York since 1871.
Saint Rosalie Interceding for the Plague-stricken of Palermo
3960488: Drunken Silenus is a 1620 painting by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister in Dresden.
3998985: Charles I in Three Positions, also known as the Triple Portrait of Charles I, is an oil painting of King Charles I of England painted in 1635–1636 by the Flemish artist Sir Anthony van Dyck, showing the King from three viewpoints: left full profile, face on, and right three-quarter profile.
3998989: The Triple Portrait of Henrietta Maria is a 1638 painting by Anthony van Dyck depicting Henrietta Maria of France, wife of Charles I of England.
6828626: The Portrait of Olivia Porter is an oil painting on canvas by Anthony van Dyck, showing Olivia, Lady Porter, the wife of Sir Endymion Porter, daughter of John Boteler, 1st Baron Boteler of Bramfield, and niece of the Duke of Buckingham, a zealous Roman Catholic and a lady in waiting to Henrietta…
7232302: Portrait of Queen Henrietta Maria, as St Catherine is a painting by Sir Anthony van Dyck.
Portrait of Queen Henrietta Maria, as St Catherine
9333311: Samson and Delilah is a 1620 painting by Anthony van Dyck.It was heavily inspired by his tutor Rubens's version of the same subject and for a long time was attributed to Rubens.
11729456: Jupiter and Antiope is a series of two similar oil-on-canvas paintings by the late Baroque Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck, from c. 1620. One painting is in the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts, Ghent; the other in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum, Cologne.
11784782: The Brazen Serpent is an oil painting on canvas executed ca. 1618–1620 by the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck, now in the Museo del Prado in Madrid. It shows the Biblical story told in Numbers whereby Moses raised a bronze image of a serpent to the Israelites.
15553205: Magistrate of Brussels is an unfinished oil painting or oil sketch by Anthony van Dyck, rediscovered in 2013 after being shown on episodes of the BBC television programme Antiques Roadshow.
16038543: The Vision of the Blessed Hermann Joseph, or The Mystical Engagement of the Blessed Hermann Joseph to the Virgin Mary, is a 1629-1630 painting by the Flemish Baroque painter Anthony van Dyck.
The Vision of the Blessed Hermann Joseph
16155993: Entry of Christ into Jerusalem is a 1617 oil painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck, located in the Indianapolis Museum of Art in Indianapolis, Indiana. It depicts Jesus entering Jerusalem as described in the Gospels, the event celebrated on Palm Sunday.
Entry of Christ into Jerusalem (van Dyck)
17036474: Magistrates of Brussels was a 1634–35 oil painting by Anthony van Dyck. It was destroyed in the French bombardment of Brussels in 1695.
18419520: Diana and a Nymph Surprised by a Satyr is a 1622–1627 oil on canvas painting resulting from a collaboration between Anton van Dyck and Frans Snyders.
Diana and a Nymph Surprised by a Satyr
18683279: Sir William Killigrew is a 1638 Baroque portrait of Sir William Killigrew (1606–1695) by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck. The portrait is twinned with another of his wife, Mary Hill.
18683283: Portrait of Mary Hill, Lady Killgrew is a 1638 Baroque portrait by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck. The portrait is twinned with another of the Lady's husband, William Killigrew.
Portrait of Mary Hill, Lady Killigrew
18939557: Venus Asks Vulcan to Forge Arms for her Son Aeneas or Venus at Vulcan's Forge is a 1630–1632 oil on canvas painting by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Louvre Museum, in Paris.
Venus Asks Vulcan to Forge Arms for her Son Aeneas
20083777: The Crucifixion is an oil on canvas painting by Anthony van Dyck, produced c. 1630. It is 2.51 m high.
21121912: Madonna and Child is a 1621–1627 painting by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Galleria nazionale di Parma.
21585380: The Shepherd Paris is a c.1628 painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck, dating to just after the artist's return from Italy and showing the strong influence of Titian.
21614703: The Lamentation over the Dead Christ is a painting by the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck, created c. 1629. It is now in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp.
Lamentation over the Dead Christ (van Dyck, 1629)
21614706: The Deposition or Lamentation over the Dead Christ is a painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck. Dating to 1635, it is one of his final treatments of the subject.
21716251: The Deposition is a 1619 painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck. It dates to around 1619 and reworks his 1615 version of the same subject It is held in the Ashmolean Museum, in Oxford, where it was offered by Charles T. Maude in 1869.
21745483: The Deposition or Lamentation over the Dead Christ was a painting by the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck, produced between 1629 and 1630. It measured 220 cm by 166 cm.
22329683: The Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint John and Saint Mary Magdalene is a painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck.
Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint John and Saint Mary Magdalene
22329816: The Deposition or Lamentation over the Dead Christ is a c. 1618-20 painting by the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck. It is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, in Vienna, which it entered in 1720.
22329818: The lamentation of Christ is a painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck dated to 1628-1630. It is in the collection of the Alte Pinakothek in Munich.
The Lamentation of Christ (Anthony van Dyck, Alte Pinakothek)
22329820: The Lamentation over the Dead Christ is a 1634-40 painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck. One of his last treatments of the subject, it is now in the Bilbao Fine Arts Museum, having entered it in 1985.
Lamentation over the Dead Christ (van Dyck, 1640)
22329830: St Martin Dividing his Cloak is a painting by the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck dated around 1618, which is an altarpiece in the Sint-Martinuskerk in Zaventem, Belgium. The painting portrays the story of Saint Martin sharing his cloak with a beggar.
Saint Martin Dividing his Cloak (van Dyck)
22329839: The Mocking of Christ is an oil-on-canvas painting by the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck (1599–1641) held in the Princeton University Art Museum.
22329840: Thetis Receiving the Weapons of Achilles from Hephaestus is a 1630–1632 painting in the workshop of the Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck. It was acquired by Archduke Leopold Wilhelm of Austria and is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
Thetis Receiving the Weapons of Achilles from Hephaestus
22329872: The Self-portrait is a self-portrait by Anthony van Dyck, produced around 1640. It was purchased for the National Portrait Gallery, London in 2014.
24668312: Saint Rosalia Crowned by Angels is an oil on canvas painting by the studio of Anthony van Dyck, created c. 1624, one of several works showing the saint produced whilst van Dyck was quarantined in Palermo, Sicily due to a plague.
26526455: Portrait of François Langlois is a Portrait painting by the 17th century Flemish Painter Anthony Van Dyck.
27699878: Saint Rosalia is a c.1625 oil on canvas painting by Anthony van Dyck. Originally owned by Giovan Francesco Serra di Cassano, it was bought by Philip IV of Spain via his Viceroy of Naples Gaspar de Bracamonte in 1664 and is now in the Museo del Prado in Madrid.
27981782: The Coronation of Saint Rosalia or Madonna and Child with Saints Rosalia, Peter and Paul is an oil on canvas painting made by Anthony van Dyck in 1629.
28026253: The Three Eldest Children of Charles I is an oil painting on canvas by Anthony van Dyck, produced between November 1635 and March 1636 and still in the Royal Collection. Numerous studio copies were made of this painting.
The Three Eldest Children of Charles I (Royal Collection)
29871346: Susanna and the Elders is an oil on canvas painting by Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck, created c. 1621-1622. It is held now in the Alte Pinakothek, in Munich, which acquired it in 1806 from the Düsseldorf Gallery.
29902758: The Virgin Presenting Saint Rosalia to the Trinity is an oil on canvas painting, now in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich. Its poor condition makes attribution difficult, but it is usually attributed to Anthony van Dyck in his Sicilian period (1624-1625).
The Virgin Presenting Saint Rosalia to the Trinity
38395329: Luigia Cattaneo-Gentile, also known as A Noblewoman from Genoa, is a portrait painting by the Flemish Baroque painter Anthony van Dyck. It is on display in the Musée des Beaux-Arts of Strasbourg, France.
47498729: The Apostle Matthew is a c. 1618-1620 painting by the Flemish artist Anthony van Dyck depicting Matthew the Apostle. One of its inspirations was probably the series of paintings of the Apostles he had seen in his master Rubens' studio around 1610, produced for the Duke of Lerma.
52252296: The Portrait of Sir Robert Shirley is a painting by Sir Anthony van Dyck, a Flemish Baroque artist. It is a portrait of Sir Robert Shirley, the ambassador to the Safavid Shah Abbas I, beginning in 1608.
61272133: The Portrait of Lady Shirley is a 1622 painting by Sir Anthony van Dyck, a Flemish Baroque artist. It is a portrait of Teresa Sampsonia (1589–1668), a Circassian noblewoman of the Safavid Empire of Iran.
65146651: Madonna with Partridges or Rest on the Flight into Egypt is a 1632 oil on canvas painting by Anthony van Dyck, with animals painted by Paul de Vos. It is now in the Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg, Russia.
87998055: A Soldier on Horseback is a c. 1616 painting by Flemish painter Anthony van Dyck. It was held at Christ Church Picture Gallery until its theft in March 2020.
88802733: Saint Rosalia Crowned by Angels is a c. 1625 oil on canvas painting by Anthony van Dyck, one of five surviving works showing the saint which he produced whilst he was quarantined in Palermo, Sicily due to a plague. It is now in the Menil Collection in Houston, Texas, which bought it in 1968.
88851112: Saint Rosalia Crowned by Angels is a c. 1625 oil on canvas painting by Anthony van Dyck, one of five surviving works showing the saint which he produced whilst he was quarantined in Palermo, Sicily due to a plague. It is now in the Wellington Collection at Apsley House in London.
88854788: Saint Rosalia Interceding for the City of Palermo is an oil on canvas painting of Saint Rosalia by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Museo de Arte de Ponce in Puerto Rico, which acquired it at auction at Sotheby's in London on 7 December 1960.
Saint Rosalia Interceding for the City of Palermo
89354668: The Three Eldest Children of Charles I is an oil painting on canvas of 1635 by Anthony van Dyck in the Galleria Sabauda in Turin.
The Three Eldest Children of Charles I (Turin)
89591592: The Resurrection is an oil on canvas painting completed in 1631 - 1632 by Anthony van Dyck, now in the Wadsworth Atheneum, in Hartford, Connecticut. Experts date the painting to Van Dyck's second Antwerp period, around 1627‐32.
89978935: Mary Villiers, Lady Herbert of Shurland is a c. 1636 oil painting on canvas by Anthony van Dyck. It is a portrait of Mary Stewart, Duchess of Richmond as a young widow, before she married for the second time to the Duke of Richmond.
Mary Villiers, Lady Herbert of Shurland
